answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a karst as the anchor of the cost.
